what: Robinhood runs a commission-free brokerage app. It earns money by routing orders to market makers, lending cash and shares, charging for its Gold subscription, and from crypto trading, retirement accounts and a credit card.
customers: Individual investors in the United States and, increasingly, other countries, skewed toward younger first-time investors.
money: payments from market makers for routing options, equity and crypto orders
interest on customer cash, margin lending and securities lending
Gold subscriptions, the credit card and matched retirement contributions
moat: A brand and interface that brought a generation into investing, with the lowest cost of acquiring a new customer among US brokers.
risks: Revenue depends heavily on options and crypto trading, which collapse in quiet markets
Regulators have repeatedly examined payment for order flow
Interest income falls when central banks cut rates
Customers are younger and have smaller balances than at traditional brokers
opportunities: Revenue grew about 52% in the last financial year
Retirement accounts and the Gold subscription build recurring revenue
Expansion into prediction markets and international brokerage adds new lines
watch: Net deposits and Gold subscriber numbers, which show whether balances are getting stickier.
